To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose an algorithm for multi-instance classification of gigapixel resolution images, 2) we apply our algorithm to the classification of glioblastoma and low-grade glioma subtypes and achieve an accuracy of 96.8%, 3) we attempt the classification of the three most common low-grade glioma types and achieve an accuracy that is similar to the agreement between experienced pathologist.
we have developed the first multiple instance convolutional neural network (MIL-CNN) for multi-gigapixel image classification.
we propose a new framework to combine Multiple Instance Learning and Convolutional Neural Network for multi-gigapixel resolution image classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of image classification on multi-gigapixelscale images and videos.
the application of CNNs to the analysis of large-scale medical image data, where the training data is too big for CNNs to handle.
the development of a new method for image classification, where we combine CNNs with MIL to handle multi-gigapixel image data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method can achieve the accuracy comparable to that of human pathologists.

the CNNs are able to classify glioma subtypes with a high accuracy, even though the classification is not as accurate as the inter-observer classification between experienced pathologists, and the classification of LGG subtypes is still a challenging task.
we have developed a method to classify glioma subtypes with a high accuracy and we have demonstrated that our method is able to classify the three LGG subtypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that CNN can be applied to multi-gigapixel image data and achieve comparable results with the interobserver agreement between experienced experts.
, for the first-time, we are able to perform classification tasks at the image level for multi-gigapixel resolution images.
we have developed an efficient algorithm to classify gigapixel images and have demonstrated that the classification results are comparable to the inter- observer agreement among pathologists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MIL can be used to train a CNN with gigapixel resolution images.
CNNs trained on discriminative patches can be used for high resolution image classification.
the proposed method can be applied to any classification problem that has a large number of instances per class, and can be easily integrated into any CNN framework.
